text: Designing a good REST API is like building a clear map for developers. First, use logical, noun-based endpoints, such as `/users` or `/orders`, rather than verbs like `/getUser`. This keeps things intuitive. Second, rely on standard HTTP status codes—`200` for success, `404` for not found, and `400` for bad requests—so clients know exactly what happened. Third, always provide thorough documentation, including examples and error messages. Good docs save hours of confusion. Finally, practice versioning, for instance by adding `/v1/` to your URL path. This allows you to change the API later without breaking existing apps. These simple habits make your API robust, friendly, and long-lasting.
